<!--
Source: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville (2016), Deep Learning,
section 4.3, p. 93 (states that all local minima of a convex function
are global); Murphy (2012), section 7.3.3, p. 222 (convex functions
have a unique global minimum when strictly convex).
The proof is the standard argument from the chord inequality.
-->
:::{#exm-convex-local-global}
#### A convex and a non-convex function

$f(x) = (x - 2)^2$ is convex (@def-convex-function):
by expanding the square,
$f(t x + (1 - t) y) - t f(x) - (1 - t) f(y) = -t (1 - t) (x - y)^2 \le 0$.
Its local minimizer $x^* = 2$ is also a global minimizer,
since $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 \ge 0 = f(2)$ for every $x$.

Without convexity, this can fail:
$f(x) = x^3 - 3x$ is not convex (@exm-cubic-not-convex),
and it has a local minimizer at $x^* = 1$
that is not global (@exr-local-vs-global-min).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-convex-local-global}
#### Local minimizers of convex functions are global

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ be a
[convex function](#def-convex-function).
Every [local minimizer](#def-local-minimizer) of $f$
is a [global minimizer](#def-global-minimizer) of $f$ over $\reals^p$.

:::
